episodes.169275: Afternoon heating brought scattered showers and thunderstorms. Plentiful moisture in these storms resulted in localized flash flooding.
episodes.169293: A persistent pattern continued on June 30, 2022, as an area of high pressure to the east of New Mexico allowed for a deep moisture plume across the area. With this moisture plume focused across western New Mexico, the afternoon and evening thunderstorms favored areas along and west of the central mountain chain. The Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon burn scar, which for several days had received steady, stratiform rain, finally responded as heavy rain resulted flash flooding and debris flow on the northern end of the large burn scar in Mora County.
episodes.169473: A line of severe thunderstorms tracked east-northeast from far northeastern Wyoming and southeastern Montana across northwest South Dakota. The storms produced wind gusts near 70 mph.
episodes.169477: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms developed across south central South Dakota, producing wind gusts over 70 mph.
episodes.169478: A thunderstorm became severe over northwestern Harding County and moved northeast into North Dakota. The storm produced large hail in the Ladner area.
episodes.169482: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over northwestern Harding County, producing hail to golf ball size west of Ladner.
episodes.169506: A weak cold front moved through southern New England and triggered scattered showers and thunderstorms.  A lightning strike caused minor damage in northeast Massachusetts.
episodes.169554: Afternoon and evening sea breeze thunderstorms produce gusty winds over the coastal waters.
episodes.169555: Lightning strike injures one near Gibsonton in Hillsborough County.
episodes.169740: An isolated thunderstorm that moved offshore and over the Cape in Brevard County produced a couple of strong wind gusts.
episodes.169741: A thunderstorm just north of the Treasure Coast Airport in Fort Pierce produced a brief tornado over an unpopulated wooded area.
episodes.170236: Two clusters of eastward-moving strong to severe thunderstorms developed during the evening of the 29th. The first was associated with weak low pressure across south central South Dakota, and the second was triggered by a cold front across north central South Dakota, both in hot environments with daytime highs in the 90s. These storms produced 60 to 70 mph or greater wind gusts, including 68 mph six miles southwest of the Joe Creek Rec Area, and damaged trees and other property across the area. High non-thunderstorm winds developed across east central South Dakota during the evening as well, the highest measured being 63 mph four miles west of Bryant.
episodes.170312: Light southeast steering flow prevailed across the area with a prevailing east coast sea breeze regime with an inverted surface trough across the local area. The combination of diurnal instability and convergence along the trough axis produced a few strong to severe storms across inland areas.
episodes.170346: Between the late afternoon of Thursday the 30th and the early morning of Friday July 1st, numerous showers and mainly weak thunderstorms occurred within this six-county North Central Kansas area. Mainly between 6-7 p.m. CDT, a small line of storms briefly became strong to marginally-severe over northern portions of Smith and Jewell counties, with a mesonet station eight miles north of Bellaire measuring a gust of 58 MPH. Heavy rain also affected a small portion of the area. Aided by an increased southwesterly low-level jet during the evening, a very narrow west-east oriented band of moderate to heavy rain set up directly along the Kansas-Nebraska state line, with the brunt of accumulation occurring prior to midnight CDT. Although there were no known gauge readings within the North Central Kansas portion of this heavy rain stripe, radar estimation and a few measurements just over the state line in Superior NE strongly suggest that at least 2-3 inches fell across the extreme northern fringes of Jewell County.||Upper level flow across the Central Plains was westerly, as the region resided on the southern side of a larger scale low pressure system working its way east across Canada. An accompanying area of low pressure at the surface deepened as it shifted east into Ontario during the daytime hours, with a southward trailing cold front sliding through the Northern and Central Plains. By late afternoon, this cold front was draped from eastern NE into west-central KS, working into and stalling over North Central Kansas. Though better overall upper level lift was north of the region, thunderstorms were able to fire along this boundary locally. Mixed-layer CAPE peaked between 1000-2000 J/kg, but deep layer shear was on the lower side, around 30 knots.
episodes.170564: Showers and thunderstorms developed over areas with large dew point depressions. The result was isolated strong, brief outflow wind gusts.
episodes.170655: A severe thunderstorm produced an isolated but intense microburst wind gust to 74 mph east of Centennial.
episodes.170659: Severe thunderstorms dropped large hail and caused damaging winds over portions of west and central Upper Michigan during the evening of the 30th.
episodes.170946: A warm front moving across the Northland lead to the development of afternoon showers and thunderstorms across the region. Later that evening a very strong low level jet brought increasing moisture into the area leading to the development of elevated storms that produced hail. The largest hail was around two inches in diameter.
episodes.170978: Scattered thunderstorms developed across the higher terrain of the High Plains and moved into central South Dakota during the evening of June 29th. Despite weak instability, deep inverted-V soundings resulted in DCAPE values of 1000-1500 J/kg, allowing for isolated damaging wind gusts with the strongest storms.
episodes.171203: A weak cold front drifted into the region while a series of upper disturbances moved across the region. This produced multiple rounds of mainly afternoon storms, some of which became severe.
episodes.171205: A waterspout was reported from an offshore rig.
episodes.171267: Moisture associated with Potential Tropical Cyclone Two resulted in shower and thunderstorm formation across the interior and western Puerto Rico. Heavy showers caused urban and small stream flooding in some municipalities.
episodes.171271: Thunderstorms developed along and in the vicinity of a frontal boundary that lifted into southern North Dakota as a short-wave trough approached the area. Initial severe storms over Bowman County produced one-inch diameter hail, then the main threat shifted towards severe wind gusts. Over LaMoure County, in the Berlin and Grand Rapids areas, significant tree damage was reported with estimated wind gusts of 90 mph.
episodes.171426: A thunderstorm produced heavy rain and flash flooding in and around Clarkdale.
episodes.171435: A cold front moving across the Upper Great Lakes produced strong to severe thunderstorms across much of Lake Superior during the evening of the 30th.
episodes.171464: A complex of strong to severe thunderstorms developed across the Lower Arkansas River Valley and moved eastward, directly along Highway 50. A few severe thunderstorm wind gusts were reported.
episodes.171502: Scattered showers and thunderstorms in the Florida Keys coastal waters were embedded in weak east to southeast lower tropospheric flow, and resulted in isolated gale-force wind gusts outside Key West's Northwest Channel.
episodes.171560: Thunderstorms moved west across southeast Arizona. Thunderstorm winds downed power lines in Patagonia while heavy rain caused flash flooding in the Baboquivari Mountains.
episodes.171743: Several lightning strikes caused damage in southwest Alabama.
episodes.171744: Heavy rain caused flooding in the western Florida panhandle.

episodes.171841: An increase of monsoonal moisture resulted in multiple storms with microburst wind gusts in northern Utah, as well as flash flooding in portions of southern Utah.
episodes.171875: Another active afternoon and evening of summertime convection produced reports of scattered wind damage, quarter size hail, and  0.50 to 2.0 inches over portions of north and central Georgia, with the highest amounts observed over the west Atlanta metro. These amounts of 1.5 to 5 inches occurred in Carroll and Douglas county, and were enough to cause flash flooding in the latter.
episodes.171877: Severe thunderstorms impacted portions of the region during the late evening and early overnight hours, bringing primarily damaging wind gusts and heavy rain.
